locations.statement: Definition of C_{i,m} and C_{1,1} comparable to rank
Action-based restatement and finiteness for all hyperbolic groups

findings.claim: The definition requiring pi_1(Lbar)=G does not yield a finite C_{1,1}(G) for general finitely generated hyperbolic groups.
findings.proof: A one-dimensional simplicial complex is a graph, so its fundamental group is free. For G=pi_1(Sigma_2), rank(G)=4 and H_2(G;Z)=Z, whereas free groups have H_2=0. Thus no admissible graph exists and C_{1,1}(G)=infinity. For F_d, d>=1, a graph consisting of d triangles sharing one vertex gives d <= C_{1,1}(F_d) <= 1+5d <= 6d; the trivial group requires 1+rank. The action-based definition on p.25 differs at m=1 because a connected free G-graph need not be a universal cover.
findings.counterevidence: For m>=2, the connectivity requirement makes the free action formulation agree with the universal-cover formulation. The main theorem uses C_{2,m}, m>=2.
findings.impact: The introductory low-dimensional identification and unrestricted finiteness assertion are incorrect under the printed definition; no main complexity estimate is contradicted.
findings.repair: Restrict the rank comparison to nontrivial free groups, or separately define the m=1 action-based complexity. Explicitly use m>=2 for the main invariant.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: Printed m=1 definition still requires pi1(Lbar)=G. Closed genus2 surface group is one-ended hyperbolic and has rank4.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: Every connected one-dimensional simplicial complex is a graph with free fundamental group; the surface group has H2=Z, so no admissible graph exists. C_(1,1)=infinity cannot compare to rank4. For nontrivial F_d the d-triangle graph gives d<=C<=1+5d<=6d.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_scope: Action-only m1 formulation differs from universal-cover definition. For m>=2 simple connectivity makes the formulations agree. Principal C_(2,m) estimate uses m>=2 and is not contradicted.
independent_acceptance_check.repair: Restrict rank comparison to nontrivial free groups, or explicitly separate the m1 action invariant.

locations.statement: Cayley graph application of Theorem B
Free geometric action and one barycentric subdivision

findings.claim: One subdivision need not make the quotient simplicial; an ordinary undirected Cayley action with involutions is not free on the realization.
findings.proof: Translation by Z on the simplicial integer line is free. After one barycentric subdivision the quotient has two vertices and two distinct edges with the same endpoints, hence is not an abstract simplicial complex. A second subdivision yields a four-cycle. The same generator-loop issue occurs for a torsion-free surface-group Cayley graph. For G=pi_1(Sigma_2) x C_2, an included involution s reverses the edge {1,s} and fixes its midpoint; G is one-ended and hyperbolic, and subdivision does not remove this fixed point.
findings.counterevidence: The paper defines free actions geometrically, and its later Rips target is explicitly only proper. The finite-stabilizer version of the resolution argument is valid; torsion is not a counterexample to Theorem A.
findings.impact: The particular graph choice on p.4 does not satisfy the stated convention for all groups. Both convention problems admit a fixed graph replacement preserving the exact index scaling.
findings.repair: Choose a finite genuine simplicial presentation complex P for G and let X' be the one-skeleton of its universal cover. The deck action is free and cocompact, X'/G=P^(1) is simplicial, X' is quasi-isometric to G, and Vol(X'/H)=[G:H]Vol(X'/G) for every finite-index H. Thus the conclusion of Theorem C is unchanged, with constants depending on the fixed model.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: Geometric rather than vertex-only freeness; abstract simplicial quotient convention.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: Integer-line Z translation after one barycentric subdivision has quotient with two vertices and two parallel edges. For pi1(Sigma2)xC2 with involution generator, left multiplication reverses{1,s} and fixes its midpoint; subdivision does not remove that fixed point.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: An oriented CW Cayley convention can avoid the second reading; make the model explicit. A finite genuine simplicial presentation complex P has free deck action on the1-skeleton X' of its universal cover; X' is proper/cocompact and quasi-isometric to G. Vol(X'/H)=[G:H]Vol(X'/G) exactly. This gives the needed TheoremB?C argument with a fixed model, without a torsion counterexample to rigidity.

findings.claim: The subgroup index formula used in the proof applies to k nonzero, not every integer k.
findings.proof: Under the literal cyclic-subgroup notation, <phi^0> is trivial, so F_d semidirect <phi^0>=F_d is the kernel of G -> Z and has infinite index, not |0|=0. For the usual nontrivial atoroidal setting d>=2, a nonzero-power mapping torus has Euler characteristic 0, while chi(F_d)=1-d is nonzero. Hence the omitted zero case can be proved separately. If both exponents vanish the conclusion is immediate; opposite nonzero exponents are handled by inverting the stable letter.
findings.counterevidence: No counterexample to the corollary in its usual nontrivial atoroidal range is asserted. The substantive finite-index argument works for all nonzero powers.
findings.impact: A boundary case is omitted from the written proof; this does not damage the finite-index rigidity theorem.
findings.repair: State m,n in Z minus {0}, or add the Euler-characteristic argument for zero powers. Clarify whether the notation denotes the cyclic subgroup or a mapping torus with an abstract infinite cyclic factor.

independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: Under literal subgroup notation <phi^0> is trivial; F_d is the mapping-torus kernel and has infinite index, not0.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: Nonzero powers have the stated finite index. In the usual nontrivial atoroidal range d>=2, chi(F_d)=1-d while nonzero-power mapping tori have chi0, excluding mixed zero/nonzero isomorphisms. Both-zero and opposite-nonzero cases are immediate. Abstract infinite-cyclic mapping-torus notation for phi^0 is a different convention that must be stated.

locations.statement: Full contractible Rips complex and application to (8.3)

findings.claim: The full Rips target need not have dimension m; the Section8 application omits the standard instruction to use its m-skeleton and the corresponding cellular extension.
findings.proof: For a closed surface group m=dim(boundary)+1=2. In a Rips complex of sufficiently large radius d>=3, four consecutive vertices on a geodesic span a 3-simplex, so the full target can have dimension at least 3. This invalidates the dimensional inference, but is not a counterexample to the quas-surjectivity conclusion.
findings.counterevidence: Set Z=Y_full^(m), m>=2. It has the same1-skeleton,boundary,proper/cocompact action and is(m-1)-connected since Y_full iscontractible. A relative equivariant cellular extension from free m-dimensional L liesinZ. Controlled relative equivariant cellular approximation in uniformlybounded simplicialstars preserves(8.2) up to aconstant ofthefixed locallyfinite finite-dimensionaltarget; auxiliarysubdivision onlyconstructsthemap anddoesnotchangecomplexityorpatterncounts. Proposition7.1 applies verbatimtoZ and sufficesfor(8.3). Section8upperbound alreadyusesanexplicitm-skeleton. The retained full-target cohomology argument is additional counterevidence.
findings.impact: Omitted standard target specification, not a newly established unclosed cohomological obstruction or a counterexample to the main lower bound.
findings.repair: Specify Z=Y_full^(m) and choose the equivariant cellular extension relative to the selected geodesic edges. Apply Proposition7.1 to Z; its conclusion on the common1-skeleton gives the needed estimate with constants dependingonlyon thefixedtarget. No newgroupassumption or asymptotic bound. The prior full-target vanishing/naturality proof remains a valid alternative.
findings.severity_basis: Minor rests on the precise standard skeletal interpretation of the construction and its preserved hypotheses/controlled geometry, not on repairability alone or absence of a main-theorem counterexample.
